Rename a symbol across its definition, call sites, and import statements.

Usage: normalize edit rename [OPTIONS] [target] [new-name]

Arguments:
  [target]    Target symbol (path/Symbol)
  [new-name]  New name for the symbol

Options:
      --dry-run                    Dry run - show what would change
      --jsonl                      Output one JSON object per line (for arrays)
      --pretty                     Human-friendly output with colors and formatting
      --compact                    Compact output without colors (overrides TTY detection)
      --force                      Proceed even when name conflicts are detected
      --json                       Output machine-readable JSON
      --jq <jq>                    Filter output through jq expression
  -m, --message <message>          Message for shadow history
      --input-schema               Print JSON Schema of the subcommand's input parameters and exit
  -r, --root <root>                Root directory
      --output-schema              Print JSON Schema of the subcommand's return type and exit
      --params-json <params-json>  Provide all parameters as a JSON object instead of individual flags
  -h, --help                       Print help

Uses the facts index to find cross-file references. If the index is unavailable,
falls back to renaming only the definition.

Aborts if the new name already exists as a symbol in the definition file or as
an import in any affected file. Use `--force` to override conflict checks.

Examples:
normalize edit rename src/lib.rs/old_name new_name             # rename across all references
normalize edit rename src/lib.rs/old_name new_name --dry-run   # preview rename changes
normalize edit rename src/lib.rs/old_name new_name --force     # ignore name conflicts
